problem: TargetResolver is a resource-layer boundary but lazily imports current_runtime_registry from modules when no registry is supplied. modules already depends on resources, so this hidden service locator reverses the intended dependency direction and keeps resources in the main SCC.

options.name: Keep the lazy global RuntimeRegistry lookup
options.correctness: Preserves call-site convenience but hides a composition dependency inside resources and leaves the 11-package SCC unchanged.

options.name: Require ResourcePluginRegistry at TargetResolver construction
options.correctness: Keeps target validation identical while making the dependency visible at application/module call sites that already own or can access the composed RuntimeRegistry.
options.complexity: Eight governed paths including four production call sites/tests, one cumulative ratchet, one boundary regression and one responsibility record.
options.migration: Record expected-red, make TargetResolver constructor explicit, pass the existing composed resources registry from each approved call site, and make the B3 count assertion monotonic.
options.rollback: Restore the optional constructor and lazy modules import, revert call sites and the exact B3 count.
options.verification: Target resolution tests, Architecture Gate, full Quick, lifecycle and Chromium.

options.name: Create a new global resource registry provider inside resources
options.correctness: Removes the import edge but preserves the hidden service-locator behavior and creates another mutable global authority.
options.migration: Add provider configuration and implicit fallback.
options.rollback: Remove provider and restore modules lookup.
options.verification: Would need provider lifecycle and concurrency certification.

rejected_reasons.keep-hidden-runtime-registry: It preserves the reversed dependency and hidden composition lookup.
rejected_reasons.resource-global-provider: It would improve the graph only cosmetically while retaining a service locator and creating another global mutable authority.

deletions: The lazy import of agent_core.modules.current_runtime_registry is removed from agent_core.resources.targets; no ResourcePlugin or target-set behavior is deleted.
unknowns: The remaining 10-package SCC remains open debt.
Real model certification remains outside this structural migration.
selected_responsibilities: agent_core.resources owns resource contracts and target validation without knowing application composition.
Application and installed business-module call sites supply the already composed ResourcePluginRegistry explicitly.
agent_core.modules/composition continue to own registry construction and installation.
preserved_hard_invariants: ResolvedTargetSet fields, canonical ordering, evidence and scope verification remain unchanged.
Every target resource type is still validated through ResourcePluginRegistry.require.
Operation capability and transaction behavior remain unchanged.
ledger, rag and utils remain outside the main SCC.
The dependency debt baseline is not edited.
cutover_strategy: Create the red architecture contract before implementation, make constructor injection mandatory, update only known call sites to pass their existing registry, then run complete product verification.
acceptance_claims: resources has no modules import and is absent from the main SCC.
TargetResolver cannot be constructed without an explicit ResourcePluginRegistry.
The current SCC member count is 10 and cannot regress above prior verified bounds.
Target resolution, transaction, frontend, lifecycle and browser behavior remain green.
